item.description:
Robbie Williams "BRITPOP (Deluxe Edition)"
Dolby Atmos Music



Britpop is the thirteenth studio album by English singer-songwriter Robbie Williams, and his first studio album since 2019's The Christmas Present. The album was released on 16 January 2026 by Columbia Records. It produced five singles: "Rocket" featuring Black Sabbath guitarist Tony Iommi, "Spies", "Human" featuring Mexican pop duo Jesse & Joy, "Pretty Face" and "All My Life". The album earned favourable reviews from music critics.

Public comments from Williams and his collaborators indicate that Britpop began taking shape early 2024, with the project developing alongside planning for Williams’ biopic Better Man. In September 2024, Williams said he had been recording extensively all year but was waiting to lock in release plans around the film before committing to a full album rollout.[2]

Later September 2024, his drummer and collaborator Karl Brazil stated that Williams worked with Tony Iommi on a rock track that would later be released as “Rocket”, signalling that recording and writing sessions were still underway by autumn 2024

item.title: 【Albums (lossy)】Dolby Atmos - Armin van Buuren "Breathe" [Dolby Atmos, 5.1, 48.0 kHz, 768 kb/s]
item.description:
Armin van Buuren "Breathe"
Dolby Atmos Music



The album, which spans two discs, includes previously released singles ‘Sound of You’ with Pendulum's Rob Swire, ‘Is It Beautiful?’ with Ben Hemsley and Lucy Pullin, ‘Euphoria’ with Alok, Norma Jean Martine and LAWRENT, and ‘Dream a Little Dream’ with Sam Gray.

The new album also features a new single, ‘Let It Be For Love, which features vocalist and songwriter JAI RYU.

The marathon new collection also features Ferry Corsten, Hardwell, Yorkshire rapper ORKID, Moby, Bon Jovi, David Guetta, and many more.

Back in April, van Buuren announced the album on Instagram with the following statement: “As many of you know, I’ve been on a personal journey these past years. Prioritizing meditating, fitness and mental health, all while touring the world, is part of this life-changing chapter called ‘BREATHE’. The music that’s on this album reflects on this journey and creative headspace.”

Earlier this month, van Buuren launched his nine-month 2025 residency at Ushuaïa Ibiza with a marathon 6-hour set.

In March, Armin van Buuren released the 2025 edition of his annual ‘A State Of Trance’ mix and performed a set at Ultra Miami made up of exclusively his own productions.

A natural follow-up to ‘Breathe In’ in both sound and meaning, ‘Breathe Out’ sees a new, healthier and reconnected Armin van Buuren deliver the second and final part of his ninth studio album, ‘Breathe’. Inspired by a stronger sense of self, more creativity and an even more dauntless approach to studio work, the album comprises a total of 39 tracks, from chart-topping hits to surprising collaborations (e.g. Pendulum & Rob Swire, Sam Gray, Moby, Bon Jovi) and new tracks, such as ‘Let It Be For Love’ (feat. JAI RYU) and ‘Want Some More’ (feat. Sam Harper). It is chockful of sound fusions and expert songwriting, showing that a balanced mind and lifestyle can lead to wonder. “‘Breathe Out’ really shows how far I’ve come, not just as an artist, but as a person. This album is about creative freedom, living fully, and putting everything I’ve learned – especially through my journey with mental health and self-growth – into the music. In many ways, it feels like coming full circle.” – Armin van Buuren
